messages:
Maria G.: Heads up — saw p99 jump from ~220ms to ~1.1s on prod-serving during a ~3k concurrent QPS spike. Suspect KV cache churn + kernel fallback. Quick dump below.

Olivier: Can you paste the flamegraph or perf sample? Which model and kernel config were in use? :thinking_face:

Maria G.: model=gpt-small-q8, runtime=serve-v2, kernels: fused_attention=auto, matmul=auto. Hot stack samples from perf: 
```
serve_worker.cpp:handle_request
kv_cache.cpp:evict_if_needed
kv_store::lookup (miss)
attention_cuda_kernel::fallback_generic
```
Maria G.: Observed microbatch size = 4 in prod. I ran replays locally: changing microbatch -> 8 reduced p99 in this workload but throughput per-GPU dropped.

Tasha: Do we have p95/p99 across batch sizes / charts?

Maria G.: Quick local replay numbers (same request mix):
- batch=4: p50=140ms p95=280ms p99=1100ms throughput=1.0k QPS
- batch=8: p50=200ms p95=340ms p99=420ms throughput=900 QPS

Olivier: Bigger microbatch raises median but reduces tail — classic latency vs throughput tradeoff. Were evictions correlated with longer sequences or hot-key churn?

Maria G.: KV hit-rate dropped from ~98% -> ~82% when concurrency spiked; eviction rate jumped and maps to the busiest shards. Most evictions were for mid-length contexts (200-600 tokens) where we keep multiple prefixes per connection.

AJ: Did you try warming the KV (prefetching hot prefixes) or increasing resident set for hot shards?

Maria G.: Tried a short grace window (100ms) before evicting newly-inserted entries; p99 improved to ~600ms in the replay without lowering throughput. Also tried LRU tuning (increase keep count) which helped but used more memory.

PerfBot: automated run #42 summary: enabling adaptive batching + grace window reduced p99 by ~55% under churn. Full results: https://perf.internal/runs/42

Tasha: Our interactive SLO is p99 <= 500ms for the interactive tier — we breached that in the incident.

Maria G.: Proposed mitigation list: 
1) Kernel selection: pin fused_attention on Ampere/RTX to avoid fallback to generic kernels during cache miss paths.
2) Adaptive microbatch sizing: increase batch size during tail spike, cap growth to protect p50.
3) KV eviction algorithm: move from strict LRU to CLOCK-like policy + larger resident quota for hot prefixes.
4) Hot-key pinning / prefetch for top N prefixes per shard.

Olivier: For (1) we should emit a low-overhead metric for kernel fallback events (counts/min) and surface per-model. That will help attribute tail to kernel fallback instead of network.

AJ: I can prototype a control loop: observe p95 and gradually increase microbatch by 2 up to 12; safety guard: if p50 > 500ms or memory pressure > 80% then step down. Would like a short experiment in staging.

Tasha: Add metrics: kv.evict_rate, kv.hit_rate, kv.resident_count per-shard and per-model tag. Also trace-level tag when fallback kernel was chosen.

Maria G.: Opening a canary with kernel pin + adaptive batching now. DeployBot: starting canary on cluster-prod-3 (canary id c-137).

DeployBot: canary c-137 started on cluster-prod-3, 50 instances.

Maria G.: Canary results after 15m: p99 back to ~320ms, kv.hit_rate stabilized ~96%, no obvious regressions. Keeping it running for an hour and will collect flamegraphs + traces.

Olivier: Great. Make sure traces include per-request kernel path and whether the path hit an evicted prefix. We'll need that to debug further.

Maria G.: Trace tags added in canary. I'll follow up with a brief RFC that includes perf graphs, config deltas, and proposed rollout plan.

Tasha: Thanks everyone — this is critical for next week's interactive release. :thumbsup:
